ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and prospective shareholders against the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register, the South African Targeted Financial Sanctions list administered by the South African Reserve Bank, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated sanctions lists, UK OFSI consolidated lists, FATF public statements, and the FIC's administrative penalties framework. Enhanced due diligence applies to any politically exposed person (PEP), including foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Verification must include documentary evidence of identity, address, source of funds, and beneficial ownership chain up to natural persons.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in any of the 11 official languages of South Africa, provided the name is expressed in Roman script; if the name is in an official language other than English, the directors must file a verified English translation or transliteration of the name for search and identification purposes; acronyms and shortened forms must be signalled in the memorandum of incorporation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Liability limited tokens 'Limited', 'Ltd', or 'Incorporated' (if not an appropriate company type)
Words implying royal or official endorsement: 'Royal', 'Official', 'Chartered', 'Registered' unless permitted under other statutes

Financial terms: 'Bank', 'Banking', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Deposit', 'Trust', 'Mutual' (require consent from the South African Reserve Bank or the Prudential Authority under the Financial Sector Regulation Act 9 of 2017)
Medical terms: 'Medical', 'Doctor', 'Hospital' (require Health Professions Council of South Africa or Department of Health approval)
Words suggesting a connection with the United Nations, the World Trade Organization, or other international bodies
Obscene, defamatory, racial, or ethnically incendiary expressions
Names that are identical or confusingly similar to existing or abandoned reserved names on the CIPC register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 calendar days after CIPC notification of rejection, the applicant may lodge a written objection or application for reconsideration with CIPC's Name Committee under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and Companies Regulation 14. The application must state the grounds of objection, provide supporting evidence, and propose the desired name. The Name Committee will review the decision and issue a written determination. If the Name Committee upholds the rejection, the applicant may file an additional name reservation or, within 30 days of that determination, apply to the High Court of South Africa (Companies Tribunal or Court route) for judicial review under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000. The applicant may also elect to reserve a fresh proposed name within the same reservation fee basket or request an extension of a pending name reservation for a further 180 days before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office address is permissible for a private company (Pty) Ltd engaged in bulk herbal export, provided that the CIPC registered office is a physical street address in South Africa (not a post office box) where legal process can be delivered during ordinary business hours, and the virtual office provider is contractually engaged to receive and forward physical correspondence, statutory notices, and service of process. The use of a virtual office address for the registered office must not result in any misrepresentation of the entity's principal place of business on the CIPC Public Register. The company must retain at its principal place of business the minute books, securities register, beneficial ownership register, and required accounting records under section 24 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate quantified risk: approximately 15% risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection by CIPC, SARS, or the Financial Intelligence Centre during the first three years of operation, with increased likelihood if the registered office is a virtual address, if the beneficial ownership profile changes, or if export volumes exceed the low-risk wholesale threshold.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 — ss 13 (incorporation), 14 (Notice of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), 23 (name), 30-34 (accounting records), 66-78 (board and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up or authorised capital is required for a (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; shares may be issued for nominal or nil consideration subject to the solvency-and-liquidity test (s 4); no escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers approve the incorporation of the Company as a private company (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and adopt the annexed Memorandum of Incorporation. 2. The registered office is fixed at the physical address designated in the Notice of Incorporation, and the accounting officer is appointed. 3. The subscribed shares are allotted and issued, and the first resident director and alternate are duly appointed. 4. The board authorises submission of the Notice of Incorporation to the CIPC, opening of bank accounts, and registration with SARS, and all ancillary steps for formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CoR 9.1 via the CIPC e-Services platform or through a registered service provider. Search the CIPC name register to confirm availability; submit a primary name plus one alternative. Upon approval, the Name Reservation Certificate is valid for six calendar months and may be renewed once for a further six months.
required_dossiers: Copy of the applicant/incorporator's green ID or passport
Payment proof of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of undesirability or similarity, the applicant may file a fresh CoR 9.1 within 20 business days with alternative names, or proceed with the company's registration number as name; appeal to the Companies Tribunal is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation and Supporting Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC-accredited company service provider or notary/attorney, filed with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI using the prescribed form or a bespoke MOI, defining share classes, director authority, and quorum rules. Prepare the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) listing the incorporators, first directors, and registered office; certify copies of identity documents and obtain director consent forms.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of directors' passports or IDs
Proof of registered office address (lease or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC identifies drafting defects or missing schedules, remedy by re-filing within 30 business days; any shareholder or third-party objection must be resolved before submission to avoid refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Application and Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload CoR 14.1 and the MOI on CIPC e-Services; pay the prescribed registration fee; track the application electronically. CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns a company registration number; the company becomes a juristic person on registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is flagged for non-compliance under s 14(2), withdraw and re-file the corrected CoR 14.1 within 30 business days; refusal decisions may be appealed to the Companies Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint the First Board, Accounting Officer and Open Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (director filings); commercial bank and Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) for KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural board meeting; record the first directors, designate the registered office, and appoint an accounting officer (member of SAICA/CCISA) since a private company is not required to appoint an auditor unless the MOI provides otherwise. File beneficial ownership particulars and any director changes via CoR 44.1 within 10 business days; open a corporate bank account with full FICA documentation.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution and minutes
Form CoR 44.1 (notice of director change) if needed
FICA/AML KYC documents (directors, shareholders, beneficial owners)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late director filings attract monthly penalties; remedy by filing an affidavit of good cause and CoR 44.1 promptly. Bank account refusals are escalated through the FIC's complaints channel or by presenting the company's SARS tax clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for South African Revenue Service Taxes and Customs Exporter Code
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal and Customs branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File SARS registration for Income Tax, VAT (mandatory where taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million; voluntary from ZAR 50,000), and PAYE/UIF/SDL once staff are employed. For export of dried goji berries and herbals, register as a SARS Customs Trader/Exporter to obtain a Customs Client Code and obtain applicable export authorisations.
required_dossiers: Proof of business address and bank account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS queries are cured by submitting a consolidated response letter with original verification documents via eFiling within 21 days; unresolved disputes follow the SARS Dispute Resolution Rules under Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Beneficial Ownership and Company Return Requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Disclose the beneficial ownership structure via Form CoR 45.2 within the prescribed timelines per the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022. Keep the securities register at the registered office and file the annual return before the last day of the anniversary month to maintain good standing.
required_dossiers: Supporting identity documents of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late beneficial ownership filing is a compliance offence under Schedule 1 of the Companies Act; remedy by filing the CoR 45.2 with a compliance affidavit and paying the prescribed penalty to reinstate good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (DALRRD) – Directorate: Food Safety and Plant Health, read with the Perishable Products Export Control Board (PPECB)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Facility Registration under the Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act 54 of 1972 and Section 12 Import/Export Permit under the Agricultural Product Standards Act 119 of 1990, plus PPECB Export Certification

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – e-SEA/EIA portal
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA (Scoping and Environmental Impact Report) under Listing Notice 2, Activity 14, GNR 325 for processing/storage of agricultural produce over 500 tonnes per annum; Basic Assessment under Listing Notice 1, Activity 19, GNR 327 for smaller packaging facilities; low-throughput dry/cold stores may qualify for exemption via an EIA checklist.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: COD ≤ 75 mg/l, BOD ≤ 25 mg/l, pH 6–9, TSS ≤ 25 mg/l per the National Water Act 36 of 1998 (Section 21 licence) and municipal sewer by-laws; dust/particulates ≤ 0.1 mg/m3 at the site boundary; organic wastes handled in sealed bins and removed by licensed waste carriers; HACCP records maintained for mycotoxin and micro-biological limits per R638 regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate in terms of the Fire Protection Act 59 of 2008 read with SANS 10400-TTTR; electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC) for all installations; structural load declaration by an ECSA-registered engineer for racking/storage; OHS Act 85 of 1993 workplace risk assessment, Compensation Fund registration, and first-aid/incident-management plan certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); official portal is https://www.sars.gov.za, with the transactional eFiling platform at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za. SARS Customs division administers export declarations (SAD500) and goods clearance; corporate registration is executed through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), after which SARS automatically issues the income tax reference number (taxpayer identification).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Proprietary Limited company with CIPC; receive company registration number and obtain the SARS income tax number (auto-populated via SARS/CIPC data interchange). Step 2: Register as a 'vendor' for VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act when or before taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period; submit VAT101 registration electronically on eFiling within 21 days of exceeding the threshold. Step 3: Apply for a SARS Customs importer/exporter code through the Customs account registration on eFiling to enable electronic SAD500 export declarations. Step 4: Appoint a public officer (for non-resident-controlled entities) and file the company tax returns; attach the statutory tax residency form and certificate of incorporation. Step 5: Validate the entity's bank account in SARS banking details on eFiling to allow VAT refunds for export zero-rating. Non-resident shareholders do not require local presence; the (Pty) Ltd as a South African resident is the taxpayer with entity-level status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' entity election. Statutory elective mechanisms available to a ZA (Pty) Ltd include: (i) CFC high-tax exclusion election under section 9D(9) of the Income Tax Act to relieve a controlled foreign company's income; (ii) VAT grouping election under section 70(3) of the VAT Act allowing a corporate group to be treated as a single vendor for indirect tax simplification; (iii) section 23H inventory valuation method elections; (iv) headquarter company election under section 9I for regional treasury/joint venture functions, subject to substantial shareholding and local substance tests; and (v) hybrid mismatch reporting elections under the Part IIBA rules, requiring alignment with OECD BEPS Action 2 and prescribed form reporting where a deduction/non-inclusion or double deduction outcome is intended. No 'pass-through' election is recognised for a South African incorporated company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS on a destination-principle consumption basis; no separate GST or state-level sales tax applies to cross-border bulk supply of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration arises when the value of taxable supplies exceeds or is likely to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months (s 23 VAT Act). Voluntary registration is possible if taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months exceeded ZAR 50,000 (s 23(3)). For an exporter, zero-rated export supplies are includible in the ZAR 1 million turnover measurement, so mandatory vendor status will typically be reached earlier than for purely domestic micro-enterprises. The company should register immediately upon contract conclusion if projected export turnover reaches the threshold within 12 months; failure to register attracts penalties and retrospective VAT assessment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently impose continuous transaction control (CTC) real-time fiscal stamping as in Latin America, but requires compliant electronic tax invoices and eFiling submission. A VAT tax invoice must issue within 21 days of supply and contain prescribed particulars per s 20 VAT Act, including seller VAT number, invoice number, date, full description, consideration, and the VAT charged separately; for exports the invoice must reflect 'export' and zero-rating evidence. Customs clearance is mandatory and electronic: the SAD500 export declaration is transmitted through the SARS EDI/electronic customs system; the SARS Customs risk engine may require documentary scanning and digital clearance before goods move. Exporters must also report through the SARB Financial Surveillance electronic export system (Form F/export schedules) where relevant. Records (including online invoice files, customs clearance records, commercial transport documents) must be retained for at least five years and be available for digital inspection on SARS eFiling.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies under s 11(1)(a) and s 11(1)(c) of the VAT Act to the supply of goods that are physically exported from South Africa: (i) the vendor (ZA_PTY_LTD) supplies dried goji berries/herbal botanicals under a sale agreement; (ii) the goods are removed from the Republic by the vendor or buyer within 90 days of the time of supply (or as extended under s 11(4) for classed goods); (iii) the vendor retains prescribed export documentary proof; (iv) the goods are not returned to South Africa or consumed locally. An intermediate service export (wholesale trading/packaging facilitation) may qualify under s 11(2)(l) as an exported service to a non-resident recipient where the services are for use outside SA, but commodity-sale income is classified as goods export. The company must assert the zero rate at invoicing only after obtaining the customs export log number; VAT refund claims for excess input tax are then implemented by SARS on a monthly or two-monthly basis per the vendor's filing cycle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SAD500 Customs Export Declaration (electronic SARS Customs release, containing goods description, HS classification, customs code and unique reference number; for goji berries use e.g. HS 1211 (lycium) / 0813 (dried fruit cross-check) depending on final classification)
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or multimodal transport document proving removal of goods from South Africa to the named export destination
Commercial invoice and packing list signed by the supplier and matched to the customs declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT TT credit advice and Foreign Exchange Transfer Form evidencing receipt of export proceeds through authorised dealer channels
SARB Financial Surveillance export form (Form F / electronic export schedule) confirming currency repatriation obligation
Phytosanitary / health certification and certificate of origin (for botanical exports where applicable), retained as supporting proof for customs risk clearance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may audit zero-rated export claims by matching the SAD500 declarations, bills of lading, remittance records and the VAT return; the vendor must retain full export 'proof pack' for five years. Understatement penalties under s 223-224 Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 range up to 200% of the shortfall for intentional/ gross-negligence conduct; where zero-rating is wrongly claimed, SARS claws back the difference as output VAT at 15% plus interest (at prescription rates) with a possible 'additional tax' equal to the tax under s 191 VAT Act. Fraudulent export schemes attract criminal prosecution under s 234 VAT Act: fine up to ZAR 10,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years; SARS also publishes the names of offending vendors, can revoke the vendor's registration/exporter status, and issue jeopardy assessments to attach assets before a dispute is resolved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), exercising delegated power under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, administered operationally through Authorised Dealers (registered commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand is a freely floating, market-convertible currency, but South Africa maintains a structural exchange-control environment. Current account transactions are fully liberalised and require only substantiating documentation routed through an Authorised Dealer. Capital account transactions (inward loans, share issues to non-residents, outbound investments) are subject to threshold-based reporting or prior FinSurv approval. Profit remittance (dividend distribution) to non-resident shareholders is generally executable without pre-approval provided: the investment qualifies as a direct investment (non-resident shareholding of at least 10%); the inward shareholding has been duly reported to FinSurv; the declaring company is 'financially self-financing'; and no impermissible domestic borrowing against the foreign capital (the 'local borrowing ratio' restriction) is in force. Dividends are additionally subject to the statutory 20% dividend withholding tax administered by SARS, with the net amount freely remittable through the Authorised Dealer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion ratio; South Africa abolished the fixed percentage surrender requirement. However, export proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa through an Authorised Dealer strictly within 180 days from the date of shipment (invoice date or bill of lading date as contractually evidenced). Upon repatriation, the proceeds must be credited to an Ordinary ZAR Account or, with FinSurv approval, retained in a designated Foreign Currency Account (FCA). The foreign currency may be held in the FCA but cannot be invested offshore or on-lent without Authorised Dealer/FinSurv authorisation; any unconsumed balance must be sold into the ZAR market or applied to approved trade payments. Extension beyond the 180-day rule is available only via a formal FinSurv application supported by the underlying trade terms (e.g., open-account credit exceeding 180 days).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual structure with Foreign Currency Account facility)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (FNB Business transactional suite with Trade Online and FCA window)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (Absa Business Banking Plus with Trade Finance and FCA capabilities)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury account; MEDIUM only as a supplementary receiving rail. Legal constraints are prohibitive for full reliance: offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not licensed by SARB and therefore cannot act as Authorised Dealers, cannot issue inward transfer advices satisfying SARB Balance-of-Payments reporting, and cannot complete the mandatory export-proceeds repatriation chain. The South African (Pty) Ltd remains statutorily obliged to route export receipts through a domestic Authorised Dealer within the 180-day window. EMIs may be used at the margin for buyer-side collections or embedded payments, but all proceeds must be swept to the primary domestic Authorised Dealer account before the SARB surrender/repatriation deadline. Any EMI arrangement must be disclosed to the onboarding bank to avoid anti-structuring AML triggers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (as amended) and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022, South African banks must identify and verify all directors and Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs). In practice, at least one natural-person director or key accountable individual with signing authority must attend a physical verification interview at a bank branch or with a bank-designated mobile banker or notary public. Remote/e-KYC onboarding is possible for South African-resident directors, but for a non-resident-owned entity the banks uniformly require an in-person compliance interview for the principal director/UBO, with certified, apostilled identity documents, a board resolution approving account opening, and a completed Beneficial Ownership register. No purely offshore 'remote-only' opening is operationally available for this entity profile; a South African resident director or a designated accountable representative must be present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with minimal local economic substance (shell-like structure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC registration certificate and Memorandum of Incorporation; Beneficial Ownership Register filed with CIPC; SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin; physical lease agreement for the registered office/warehouse; employee payroll and UIF/PAYE returns proving local substance; board resolutions appointing the South African resident director; disclosure of the full overseas shareholding chain with source-of-wealth evidence for to the shareholder injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Herbal/botanical commodity flagged for narcotics or controlled-substance misclassification (goji berry / lycium category)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PPECB (Perishable Products Export Control Board) phytosanitary certificates; SAD500 customs export declarations; independent laboratory Certificate of Analysis confirming the commodity is food-grade dried fruit and absent any controlled compounds; supplier traceability documentation from farm/grower to warehouse; material safety data sheets; International Trade Administration Act export control checks confirming no licensing prohibition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate third-party payments, cash-prepayment patterns, or divergent payment routing to non-beneficiary parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts and pro-forma invoices; supplier commercial invoices matched to the payee; bills of lading and air waybills; warehouse receipts and inspection certificates; a board-approved treasury policy prohibiting third-party disbursements; a clean audit trail of payment instruction mandates; bank-forensic documentation of the goods flow versus funds flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Prepayment or early settlement of export receivables with compressed tenors inconsistent with the agricultural trade cycle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Firm purchase orders with delivery schedules; shipping calendar and vessel booking confirmations; warehouse inventory reports; an executed hedging/forward contract with the Authorised Dealer demonstrating commercial justification for early FX conversion; and historical trade settlement records for the same buyer corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty exposure to FATF grey-listed or sanctioned jurisdictions in the buyer/supplier chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) files on all counterparties; sanctions screening logs from a reputable screening provider; country-specific end-user/customer due diligence certificates; compliance declarations from the overseas buyer; and, where applicable, OFAC/EU/SARB sanctions filter output showing negative match or favourable licensing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident parent/shareholder funds enter the company's domestic ZAR operational account via SWIFT MT103 under the SARB Balance-of-Payments classification 'equity capital (inward direct investment)'. The inbound wire must include the correct BOP purpose code for equity investment in a resident company; the receiving Authorised Dealer files the prescribed inward investment report to SARB FinSurv within 30 days of receipt. The company must simultaneously allot shares and file the special resolution with CIPC within 30 days. No prior FinSurv approval is required for an equity injection. For shareholder loans, the funds must be reported as a foreign liability on the prescribed onshore reporting template; the interest rate and terms must be arm's length and the loan must not be used to finance domestic borrowing beyond the SARB local borrowing ratio. All supporting source-of-funds evidence (audited financial statements of the lender, signed equity subscription agreement, board resolution, and share certificate) must be retained and produced to the bank on demand.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed through Authorised Dealer clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for documentary telegraphic transfers to international suppliers for dried goji berry packaging, freight, and ancillary logistics; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) opened through the corporate bank for larger, high-value shipments from overseas suppliers where documentary security is required; (3) Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) as a cost-effective alternative for established counterparties. Every outbound payment must be matched against the underlying invoice, contract, SAD500 declaration, and logistics documents, and must be captured in the Authorised Dealer's SARB monthly balance-of-payments returns. Dividend remittances to the non-resident parent are paid via SWIFT MT103 under the BOP code for dividends/distributed profits, supported by the audited dividend declaration, resolution, and exchange-control reporting form completed through the bank; the 20% withholding tax must be remitted to SARS before the net dividend is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (up to 12 months) with an Authorised Dealer against firm, committed export receivables or import payables, requiring underlying documentary proof of the exposure

Foreign currency options (purchased puts/calls) with an Authorised Dealer for premium-defined risk reduction, permissible where the underlying trade exposure is documented and matures within the option tenor

Cross-currency swaps for longer-dated structural exposures (e.g., shareholder loan repayment mismatch or multi-year supply contracts), executable only upon SARB FinSurv approval obtained through the Authorised Dealer

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing an offshore ZAR or USD/CNY fix where onshore deliverable liquidity is insufficient, permitted for hedging commodity-driven receivables when the bank confirms structural eligibility and the instrument is aligned to a firm underlying transaction
Rolling/implied forwards on approved Foreign Currency Account balances, allowing the company to lock the future ZAR value of retained export proceeds without breaching the FCA holding rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately ZAR 500 per month (approx. USD 27); persistent failure to file for two consecutive years triggers a final deregistration notice and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and board approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors; retained at registered office and presented to shareholders upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC compliance notice, administrative penalties, and potential director liability for deficient or false financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent review or statutory audit report (if triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board and shareholders; report accompanies Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed before presentation of Annual Financial Statements to shareholders; commonly within 6 months of financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or independent reviewer when required is a contravention of the Companies Act; the company may be fined and directors may be held personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and member transfer updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC through the annual return; updates recorded in statutory registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each annual return filing; all share transfers and beneficial ownership changes during the preceding year must be captured before submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update beneficial ownership details may result in rejection of the annual return, administrative fines, and sanctions under the Companies Amendment Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to public companies, state-owned companies, any company with a Public Interest Score of 350 or more, any company whose Memorandum of Incorporation requires an audit, or any company where shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights request an audit. Private companies with a Public Interest Score between 100 and 349 are subject to an independent review unless a full audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public companies and large companies with a high Public Interest Score; IFRS for SMEs may be used for smaller companies without public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and confirm beneficial ownership details in the annual return filed with CIPC. Every transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and the beneficial ownership register updated before the annual return is lodged.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Directors Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for low Public Interest Score companies; independent review USD 800–2,500; full audit USD 3,000–10,000 if triggered.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (s. 5(1)(e) Income Tax Act 58 of 1962); 28% for prior years; Small Business Corporation graduated rates up to 21% may apply if turnover ≤ ZAR 20m
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Reduced 15% SEZ rate (s. 12R) for qualifying activities in designated SEZs. 150% R&D deduction (s. 11D). 100% renewable-energy allowance (s. 12B) and 100% of costs of certain energy-efficiency savings (s. 12L). Standard commercial deductions: s. 11(a) expenses, s. 22 trading stock, s. 24J original issue discounts; group relief: s. 20(1) assessed-loss set-off cap of the greater of ZAR 1 million or 80% of taxable income (s. 20(1)(a) proviso).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime: No statutory expiry: assessed losses under s. 20 ITA are carried forward indefinitely until set off; SARS/TAA require active trade and the 80%/ZAR 1m annual offset cap for YE on/after 1 April 2022.
corporate_income_tax_regime.taxable_profit_computation: Gross income minus exempt income and allowable deductions, less assessed losses brought forward, equals taxable income; tax at 27%; foreign tax credits under s. 6quat; dividend tax withheld separately at shareholder level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via SARS eFiling; provisional returns on IRP6 (6-monthly); eFiling and SARS MobiApp. Non-resident shareholders file no SA corporate return for SA dividends; SA source passive income subject to final withholding.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be filed within 12 months of the company's year of assessment end (e.g., 31 March year-end: filed by 31 March of the following year) or the date stipulated by SARS in the notice of registration; IRP6 first provisional payment within 6 months of the start of the year, second on the last day of the year, optional third top-up within 6 months after year end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number (e.g., …/…/30/07), VAT number, SARS tax reference number, branch code; SIC/ISIC classification (4631 for wholesale of food/dried botanicals).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident Pty Ltd reports the full global taxable income; no election is available for non-resident shareholders; non-resident shareholders are not parties to the ITR14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal and secondary business codes; whether activities are conducted through a branch/PE in South Africa; commencement/cessation dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If more than 50% of the company's participatory rights are foreign-held, the company must nevertheless remain a registered taxpayer; report connected-person transactions (related non-resident suppliers/customers) in the related-party schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income: World-wide receipts and accruals in cash/kind from the sale of dried goji berries/herbal botanicals, less trade discounts; includes recoupments of capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Invoiced export sales are included in income; VAT zero-rating does not affect the ITR14 gross income. Intercompany sales to connected non-residents must be priced at arm's length (s. 31).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local dividends received (s. 10(1)(k)), certain foreign dividends (s. 10B) subject to participation exemptions, and other exempt receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividends from a group company may be exempt under the participation exemption if the shareholding threshold is met; the company must disclose the exemption claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions under s. 11(a) (expenses incurred in the production of income), s. 22 (opening/closing trading stock), s. 24J (finance charges), depreciation under s. 12C/12B, donations (s. 18A), and assessed loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in the production of South African taxable income are deductible; cross-border service fees and management charges must satisfy s. 31 arm's length and, for DPT purposes, economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equals gross income less exemptions and deductions, less any assessed loss brought forward (capped at the greater of ZAR 1 million or 80% of taxable income for years commencing on/after 1 April 2022).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident connected persons, taxable income is adjusted by SARS to the arm's length amount; the taxpayer should file an adjustment schedule and TP documentation position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at 27% on taxable income; set-off of provisional payments (IRP6), foreign tax credits under s. 6quat, and any assessed-loss offset. The net balance is payable with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If relief under a DTA applies, foreign tax credits or treaty credits are computed in this section; non-resident shareholders only interact through dividend tax declarations, not the ITR14.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative non-compliance penalty under s. 211/214 TAA (monthly, category-based: up to ZAR 16,000 per month for 'High' entities), initially escalated by ZAR amounts at SARS discretion; late payment: s. 213 TAA penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax, plus an additional 10% for each month of continuing default, capped at 100%, plus interest at the prescribed rate (repo rate plus 3.5% per annum) from the due date; understatement penalty under s. 223 TAA of 10%-150% depending on the prejudice category (substantial understatement, failure of reasonable care, unreasonable tax position, intentional evasion).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final dividends tax under s. 64EA(2) Income Tax Act, imposed on the beneficial owner of the dividend (the Pty Ltd is the withholding agent); domestic shareholder exemptions under s. 64FA (e.g., dividends to resident companies, pension funds, approved public benefit organisations) and s. 64FB (foreign companies holding ≥ 10%? actually exemption for foreign shareholder? The 20% is reduced to nil in certain cases).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a DTA reduction, the paying Pty Ltd must receive from the non-resident shareholder a completed DTR01.06 Declaration (Treaty Relief) and a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority. The declaration must be retained by the company; the reduced rate (e.g., 5%-15% for most SA treaties; often 5% for 10%+ corporate holders, 15% for portfolio investors) is applied at the moment the dividend becomes payable. If the declaration/TRC is not provided before the dividend accrual, the full 20% must be withheld and remitted to SARS, and the shareholder can reclaim over-withheld tax by filing a refund claim with SARS within 3 years (s. 99 TAA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalty WHT: 15% statutory final withholding on payments to non-residents for use of IP, know-how, etc. (s. 49A-51B ITA); treaty rates commonly 10% (some treaties 0% for equipment use or 5% for certain copyright payments). Interest WHT: 15% statutory final withholding on interest paid to a non-resident (s. 50A-50H ITA); treaty rates typically 10%, sometimes 0% for interest to financial institutions, government bodies and in some treaties (e.g., broad-based 0% interest relief). Both regimes require form R01? Actually, returns: RR (royalty) or RWT (interest) submissions via eFiling; the payer must withhold before remittance and is personally liable for unremitted WHT, with recourse against the non-resident payee.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: SARS guideline expects a Local File where cross-border connected-party transactions exceed ZAR 5 million in aggregate per annum; Master File required for MNE groups meeting the CbC threshold (consolidated group revenue ≥ ZAR 10 billion); CbC Report (BEPS Action 13) for groups with consolidated revenue ≥ ZAR 10 billion; documentation must be provided within 21 days of SARS's request and in the prescribed format (SARS Transfer Pricing Guide; Master/Local File Guideline 2016).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations are incorporated via s. 31(1) and SARS Practice Note 7
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa imposes no separate ESR statute (no UAE-style registration). Instead, substance is enforced through: (i) s. 31 arm's length control requiring conduct and substance analysis; (ii) s. 31A Diverted Profits Tax (15% additional assessment on profits diverted via arrangements lacking economic substance, effective from years ending on or after 31 December 2021); (iii) GAAR under s. 80A-80L (treating tax avoidance arrangements with no commercial substance as void); (iv) s. 103 ITA general anti-avoidance; and (v) the Companies Act corruption/self-dealing provisions (s. 20(9) piercing the corporate veil).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating export turnover, overstating trading stock/expenses, submitting false ITR14 schedules for dried herb exports, destroying books, or misleading SARS in a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TAA s. 234-235, upon conviction: fine of up to ZAR 1 million and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years; understatement penalties of up to 150% of the shortfall (s. 223); 10% monthly late-payment penalties up to 100%; interest at the prescribed rate; publication of taxpayer's name by SARS (s. 67).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who 'knowingly' participated in filing false returns or whose actions caused the company's tax default can be held personally liable for unpaid PAYE/other employees' taxes (s. 159-162 TAA); criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment; civil restitution in the amount of under-collected taxes and interest; travel bans under s. 194 TAA and attachment orders against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a zero-substance foreign intermediary in Mauritius/UAE/Hong Kong to buy, hold, or export dried goji botanicals back-to-back, stripping the SA arm of profits; commission or marketing agreements without staff, premises, or risk-bearing capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may impute arm's length profits to the SA Pty Ltd (s. 31), impose the 15% Diverted Profits Tax (s. 31A), apply GAAR invalidity (s. 80A), impose understatement penalties up to 150%, and levy interest; the intermediary's invoice deduction is disallowed in full.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For directors who form or operate the shell: piercing the corporate veil under s. 20(9) Companies Act and s. 77(3) (reckless trading) may render directors jointly and severally liable for the company's entire diverted tax debt; SARS can obtain attachment orders, DTA exchange-of-information triggers, and in aggravated cases criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dried goji berries/ herbal botanicals to a connected foreign distributor below cost or allowing excessive management/marketing fees to a foreign parent without demonstrable services, priced inconsistently with independent comparable transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjusts the transaction to arm's length under s. 31; additional CGT? no — additional income tax at 27% on the adjustment plus interest at the prescribed rate; s. 223 understatement penalty in the 10%-150% band; foreign exchange and VAT implications for the exporter; simultaneous adjustment of the PE? not automatic.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign TP schedules or approve intercompany pricing while knowing the prices are non-arm's length and cause a material shortfall face personal civil liability for the shortfall under company law, personal tax debts through SARS's third-party liability provisions, and criminal liability in flagrant evasion cases—including travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained high-value cash payments for herbal cargoes without due diligence (cash threshold reporting applies at ZAR 49,999.99 to accountable institutions), structuring cross-border Swift_TT receipts to avoid transaction monitoring, or false declarations in export invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FIC Act fines up to ZAR 10 million per contravention and imprisonment for directors who knowingly permit money laundering; Customs & Excise Act penalties for false export declarations (up to 100% of the value of goods); named on the FIC board's published list; forfeiture of proceeds under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally subject to criminal fines and imprisonment; no corporate veil protection for AML offences; travel bans and asset freezes; civil forfeiture of property involved in money laundering; SARS shares intelligence with the FIC and NPA for prosecution of directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, royalties, interest, or technical fees to non-resident shareholders/creditors without applying the required statutory or treaty withholding rates, or without obtaining the DTR01.06 declaration/TRC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Pty Ltd is personally liable for the unremitted 20% dividends tax (s. 64N), 15% royalties WHT and 15% interest WHT, plus 10% monthly penalty up to 100% and interest at prescribed rates; SARS may collect directly from the company and offset any refunds; understatement penalties for repeated neglect (s. 223).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are 'knowingly party' to a failure to withhold are jointly and severally liable for the WHT shortfall (s. 159 TAA with extension via s. 162 for employees' tax); travel bans (s. 194 TAA) and seizure of personal assets are available; criminal prosecution follows in case of intentional evasion.
